findings.text: follow-on: the mixed-resolution branch is unreachable from the production writers — the peer pointer's created_at is written by _publish_launch_claim from the dispatch's own claim_registered_at (dispatch.py:1487, :5076) and that stamp is runs._utc_now (runs.py:329, isoformat(timespec="seconds")), so both sides always carry zero fractional digits and _fractional_digits differs only in the hand-built fixture (_same_second_with_fraction). The branch is conservative (it returns refuse) so it is not a correctness risk, but the landing and fragment present the resolution rule as a production hazard; if it ever did fire symmetrically it would make both racing claims refuse, the harm the ordering exists to prevent.

follow-on: the docstring state "the same instant is written ``...T04:00:00Z`` by one caller and ``...T04:00:00.500000+00:00`` by another" — those two spellings name moments half a second apart, not the same instant, and (see above) no production caller writes the fractional form; carried from the prior review at this line.

follow-on: the third entry to _raise_repository_scope_conflict, the _raise_live_scope_conflict facade, builds its claims with the default empty registered_at and passes neither own_run_id nor own_registered_at, so the parsed-time ordering never applies at that seam; pre-existing and carried from the prior review.

follow-on: the ordering still compares wall-clock registration moments, so a later arrival from a host whose clock runs behind still ranks as the earlier one; the run-id tie-break settles only same-resolution equal instants, which the resolution guard now additionally refuses inside a second.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite, only gate.log and the negative-control logs, so the added-failure count derives as unmeasured rather than zero and the record cannot be reconciled against a base arm at a stated revision; carried from the prior review.

item_verdicts.goal: the node makes the racing-claim order read parsed registration moments and never let a newcomer outrank a run that has already passed its own admission; at head 6cf2cbc5 `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2058) returns True only when the peer claim is still composing, both stamps parse, their resolutions agree, and `(peer_instant, claim.run_id) > (own_instant, own_run_id)`; `launched` (dispatch.py:1419) is now true when the pointer carries a worktree or pid OR its phase lies outside `_UNLAUNCHED_CLAIM_PHASES` {starting, launching, launcher, dispatching}, so a running owner refuses a newcomer; a resolution mismatch inside a second returns False, keeping the peer established. justifications.durability: the guards are real and independent, verified by the three isolating negative controls, and the running-owner guard closes a genuine intermittent failure (the node's own test_crew.py runs are cited). Residual: the resolution guard's precondition cannot be produced by the production writers — both the peer pointer's created_at and the dispatch's own claim_registered_at come from the same second-precision runs._utc_now (runs.py:329) — so that branch is inert outside its hand-built fixture; the docstring's 'same instant' example and the _raise_live_scope_conflict facade gap are carried from the prior review.
justifications.evidence: strong on the guards: three negative-control logs each redden exactly one guard — restoring the raw-string comparison 2 failed/6 passed, dropping the phase term 1 failed/7 passed, dropping the resolution guard 1 failed/7 passed — so each protection fails when removed, and I reproduced the head gate independently (22 passed, EXIT=0). Two gaps: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite/after_suite, so the added-failure count derives as unmeasured (I confirmed the derivation instrument with a positive control: added_failures_from_gate_logs returned count 1, id tests/test_x.py::test_c, and None when the base log is absent); and the resolution guard's fixture shape is hand-built, not drawn from a production writer.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the existing parse_utc, the existing phase vocabulary (the launch claim already writes phase 'starting' at dispatch.py:1488) and the one shared ordering helper both admission checks call, so no second ordering implementation appears; the new module constant names a mechanism rather than a plan item.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every clause of the landing is present: the parsed-instant comparison (277f357a) is unchanged, the running-owner refusal is a real fix (a pointer whose phase is 'working' but which carries no worktree/pid — the running-pointer fixtures, and a resumed or reclaimed run — previously read as still-composing and could be outranked), and the resolution rule is present; I reproduced the head gate 22 passed / EXIT=0.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two repair commits change dispatch.py, the test file and the fragment and nothing else; the reviewed worktree is clean at head and every written path lies inside the node's declared orientation scope; no peer file is touched.
